chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Abdur Rahim Al-Qasir has been transmitted by me from Ja'far ibn Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira Al-Kufi, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir Al-Qasabani, from Abdur Rahim Al-Qasir Al-Asadi.
He was called 'Al-Asadi' because he was a freed servant (mawla) of Banu Asad.

key_terms.الأسدي: Al-Asadi, a nisba indicating affiliation with the tribe of Asad
key_terms.بني أسد: Banu Asad, the tribe of Asad
key_terms.عبد الرحيم القصير: Abdur Rahim Al-Qasir, a specific narrator
key_terms.مولى: Mawla, a freed servant or client

ai.seo_question: Why is the narrator Abdur Rahim referred to as Al-Asadi?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides this biographical note to authenticate the chain of transmission (isnad) for Abdur Rahim Al-Qasir, clarifying that his nisba 'Al-Asadi' denotes his status as a mawla of the Banu Asad tribe. This detail is crucial in Shia hadith sciences for distinguishing narrators and verifying the reliability of reports attributed to him within the broader context of the companions of the Imams.
